title: post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026
author: Aisha Raman
content:
Overview:
This document defines a repeatable post-installation acceptance and telemetry-validation checklist for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) deployments. The checklist is intended for Delivery Engineers, SREs, and Customer Success engineers performing first-day and week-1 validation after a private deployment or an infrastructure upgrade.

Scope:
- Applies to freshly provisioned control plane and runtime clusters (both VPC and air-gapped on-prem packages).
- Covers telemetry, metric baselining, log ingestion, tracing, alert sanity checks, and acceptance gates that must pass before handing over to steady-state operations.
- Does NOT replace the customer acceptance test suite; it complements that suite by focusing on observability and operational readiness.

Goals:
1. Verify telemetry completeness: key metrics, request traces, and audit logs are present and correctly attributed to the customer ID and model route.
2. Establish baseline SLO measurements and alert thresholds for the first 72 hours.
3. Validate automated rollback and fallback wiring (model variant fallback, region fallback, and canary control plane failover).
4. Capture a short runbook and signal mappings to reduce MTTD/MTTR during initial ramp.

Owner and escalation:
- Primary owner: Delivery Engineering (on-site delivery lead).
- Secondary owner: Platform SRE.
- Escalation path: Delivery Lead -> SRE on-call -> Eng Platform -> Product Security for infra anomalies.

Pre-flight checks (before committing acceptance):
- Inventory: list control plane services, runtime nodes, and versions. Example table (text):
  Table: Service | Version | NodeCount | Contact
  - control-plane-api | v2.8.1 | 3 | delivery@redwood.com
  - runtime-gateway | r-2026-01 | 6 | runtime@sre.redwood.com

- Confirm KMS/HSM integrations are bound and test-encrypted values decrypt successfully.
- Confirm NTP/time sync and FIPS mode (if required by customer) are enabled on all hosts.

Telemetry & signal checklist (execute in order):
1) Metrics ingestion sanity
   - Ensure Prometheus (or the customer-provided collector) is scraping the following endpoints: /metrics on control-plane, /metrics on runtime-gateway, and per-model-node exporters.
   - Commands to validate (examples):
     - curl -sS http://control-plane-api.internal:9100/metrics | head -n 40
     - kubectl get pods -n redwood-observability -o wide
   - Verify the following metrics exist and are updating in the metrics store:
     - redwood.requests.received_total
     - redwood.requests.latency.p50/p95/p99 (per-route)
     - redwood.kvcache.hits_total and misses_total
     - runtime.gpu.utilization_percent (per-GPU)

2) Log pipeline and retention
   - Confirm logs are flowing to the configured sink (ELK/Cloud logging/S3).
   - Verify structured logs include the fields: request_id, customer_id, model_name, model_version, route, and node_id.
   - Minimum retention validation: ensure logs are retained per the contract (e.g., 30 days for standard, 365 for compliance).

3) Tracing and distributed context
   - Fire a sample request that triggers a multi-service path (API -> Router -> Runtime -> KV cache).
   - Validate a single trace is visible in Jaeger/Tempo and contains spans for each service with correct span attributes.
   - Example curl trace invocation (with trace header):
     - curl -H 'x-trace-id: validate-123' -X POST -d '{"input":"hello"}' http://customer-gateway.internal/v1/generate

4) Audit logging and access events
   - Ensure admin actions (model roll, key rotation, route changes) are recorded to audit logs and include actor, timestamp, and IP.
   - Verify the syslog or audit sink contains a sample entry for a simulated model-version-promotion event.

Baselining and SLO measurement (first 72 hours):
- Baseline period: 72 hours of synthetic and limited real traffic. Collect greenfield baseline metrics:
  - Latency SLO targets (example): p50 < 20ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 400ms for small-text generation routes.
  - Error budget policy during onboarding: allow up to 0.5% client-visible errors for the baseline (escalate if >1%).
- Procedure:
  1. Start synthetic traffic with two profiles: low-latency probe (1 RPS per route) and load ramp (burst to expected production RPS in 5 steps).
  2. Capture percentiles and error rates every 15 minutes.
  3. If p95 exceeds baseline target for 3 consecutive 15-minute windows, pause ramp and run runtime profiling playbook.

Acceptance gates (must pass to move to steady-state handoff):
- Gate 1: Telemetry completeness: all required metrics and traces present for 24 continuous hours.
- Gate 2: Baseline SLO adherence: p95 latency within target during low-latency probes for 24 hours.
- Gate 3: No critical alerts fired for 72 hours (critical = SLO degradation, control-plane leader loss > 1 minute, persistent KV cache miss rate > 10%).
- Gate 4: Automated fallback tests succeeded (execute canary that forces model variant fallback and validate responses returned to client within SLA).

Automated validation snippets (examples to run during checks):
- Prometheus API query (p95 latency for route):
  curl -G 'http://prometheus.internal:9090/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_requests_latency_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))'

- Simple alert rule example (text description):
  - Alert name: RedwoodHighP95Latency
  - Expression: p95(route="/v1/generate") > 150
  - For: 10m
  - Severity: critical
  - Notify: SRE on-call + delivery lead

Rollback and rollback-test validation:
- Verify the deployment automation can perform a controlled rollback to the previous model/runtime revision. Test plan:
  1. Trigger a canary release to 5% of traffic.
  2. Inject a synthetic error that causes failure-rate > 5% for canary (use traffic rewriter or fault-injection in the runtime test harness).
  3. Confirm automated rollback triggers within 2 minutes and the system returns to the previous revision with no additional errors.
- Commands to validate rollback logs (example):
  - kubectl -n redwood-control logs deployment/rollout-manager | tail -n 200
  - grep "rollback initiated" /var/log/redwood/rollout-manager.log

Checklist for security and compliance signals:
- KMS rotation event logged and validated against the customer key ID.
- TLS mutual auth handshake success rate > 99.9%.
- RBAC test: attempt an action with a role below required privilege and confirm 403 logged and audited.

Operational runbook snapshot (to include in handover):
1. How to surface a late-binding model fallback: CLI example and required flags.
2. How to escalate when trace sampling drops unexpectedly.
3. Commands to increase continuous batching window (if customer desires throughput tuning).

Reporting and handover artifacts (deliver to Customer Success and SRE):
- 72-hour baseline report (PDF): includes latency percentiles, error rates, trace sample examples, and any deviations.
- Runbook excerpt: 2-page quickstart for on-call (paging thresholds, key dashboards, rollback steps).
- Evidence bundle: screenshots/links to traces, example logs, and the Prometheus query outputs used for checks.

Template: 72-hour baseline report (text layout)
- Executive summary (1 paragraph)
- Metric snapshots (table: metric, observed p50/p95/p99)
- Alerts fired (if any) and resolution status
- Action items and owners

Common failure modes and mitigations (observed in previous private deployments):
- Symptom: high p95 latency after adding larger sequence-length requests. Mitigation: pin a quantized model variant for high-seqlen or increase batch size window for low-priority routes. Owner: Runtime team.
- Symptom: missing spans in traces. Mitigation: check tracer agent sidecar, verify sampling headers are preserved across proxies. Owner: SRE.
- Symptom: audit logs not arriving. Mitigation: check forwarder credentials, rotate key if expired, and run log-forwarder debug. Owner: Security.

Appendix A: quick debug commands (examples)
- Check control plane leader: kubectl -n redwood-control get pods -l app=control-plane -o wide
- Show recent high-latency requests (example log query): jq '. | select(.level=="error" and .latency_ms>200)' /var/log/redwood/requests.log | head -n 50

Appendix B: example JSON telemetry mapping (used by delivery automation)
- Example (text): {"metrics": ["redwood.requests.received_total","redwood.requests.latency"], "labels": ["customer_id","route","model_version"]}

Appendix C: acceptance signoff checklist (one-line items for signature)
- All required metrics visible for 24h
- Traces for multi-service path verified
- Audit logs for admin actions verified
- Baseline SLOs validated for 24h
- Automated rollback tested and validated
- Delivery lead: ____________________ Date: ________
- SRE on-call: _______________________ Date: ________
